text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Eight opposition parties on Wednesday launched a public campaign aimed at ensuring the largest possible turnout at the forthcoming referenda on NATO membership and direct presidential elections. The opposition said people should vote in favour of both the integration to NATO and direct elections.

- The opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) said it was not invited to the opposition referendum campaign, but added that it was ready to start talks regarding the two plebiscites with all other opposition parties as soon as possible.
- Swedish AssiDoman Packaging said it planned to acquire 100 percent control over a major Slovak pulp and paper producer JCP Sturovo. AssiDoman already holds 91.2 percent in JCP.
- Jacobs Suchard Figaro, Slovakia's largest confectioner, posted an after-tax profit of around 83 million crowns in 1996. Figaro will not pay any dividend from last year's profit.
- The Slovak unit of German car maker Volkswagen expects its production to exceed 20 billion crowns this year, some two billion more than originally planned.
- The recently established Slovak National Airlines plans to launch operations on October 26 this year. The company said it planned to transport some 85,000 passengers by the end of 1997.
- A three-day European regional conference of Interpol will be held in Piestany, western Slovakia, beginning May 14.

PRAVDA - Agustin Marian Huska, Deputy Chairman of the Slovak parliament, has called a meeting of chairmen of all parliamentary parties to discuss members and the structure of a special parliamentary committee supervising the SIS.
- Opposition SDL has warned that bad organisation of the two referenda this month, on NATO membership and direct presidential elections, will politicaly destabilise the country.

- The Slovak parliamentary Chairman Ivan Gasporovic quoted his Polish counterpart Jozef Zych as saying that Warsaw wants Slovakia to be integrated to NATO at the same time as all other associated countries.

- The state-owned monopoly gas distributor SPP last year sold 6.6 billion cubic metres of gas. The SPP said it made no profit from sales of gas in Slovakia in 1996 and that its main revenue came from transit of Russian gas to western Europe. -- Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402
